samples.text:
The graph shows how many printed books, e-books and audiobooks were borrowed from public libraries in a town from 2012 to 2024.

Printed books were the most borrowed format in all the years. In 2012 there were 480 thousand loans, but this number decreased steadily to 380 thousand in 2018. Then in 2020 it drop suddenly to 250 thousand. After that it went up to 300 thousand in 2022 and was 290 thousand in 2024.

E-books was very low at first with only 15 thousand loans in 2012. However, it increased every year and it was 110 thousand in 2018. In 2020 it jumped to 205 thousand, which was nearly the same with printed books. It fell a little in 2022 and then reach 215 thousand in 2024.

Audiobooks were also increasing. They were 30 thousand in 2012 and 55 thousand in 2018, and then they rose to 160 thousand in 2024.

Overall, printed books decreased while e-books and audiobooks increased, and the difference between them became much smaller.
samples.why: Overview placed at the end · main trends identified with mechanical detail · limited range of vocabulary · agreement, tense and preposition errors that do not impede communication.

samples.text:
The line graph gives information about the number of library loans in a town for three different formats, printed books, e-books and audiobooks, between 2012 and 2024.

Overall, printed books remained the most borrowed format throughout, but their popularity declined considerably. Conversely, loans of e-books and audiobooks increased significantly, which meant that the gap between the formats became much narrower by 2024.

In 2012, printed books accounted for 480,000 loans, far more than audiobooks (30,000) and e-books (15,000). Borrowing of printed books then fell gradually to 380,000 in 2018 before dropping sharply to 250,000 in 2020. It recovered somewhat to 300,000 in 2022 but slipped slightly to 290,000 by the end of the period.

E-book loans, on the other hand, grew steadily, overtaking audiobooks by 2014 and reaching 110,000 in 2018. In 2020 they rose dramatically to 205,000, only 45,000 less than printed books, and after a small drop they stood at 215,000 in 2024. Audiobooks showed a slower but consistent rise, with loans increasing more than fivefold to 160,000 over the twelve years.
samples.why: Clear overview of decline versus growth · key features and the 2020 change highlighted · effective cohesion · good use of derived comparisons · mostly accurate grammar with a minor 'less/fewer' slip.

samples.text:
The graph compares the number of items borrowed from a town's public libraries in print, e-book and audiobook formats over the period 2012 to 2024.

Overall, printed books, though still the most popular format at the end of the period, saw a marked decline in borrowing, while digital and audio formats grew strongly. The most abrupt change occurred in 2020, when print loans slumped and e-book loans surged.

Printed book loans fell steadily from 480,000 in 2012 to 380,000 in 2018, before plunging to 250,000 in 2020. Although they partially recovered to 300,000 in 2022, they had eased back to 290,000 by 2024, around 40% below their initial level.

E-books, which accounted for a mere 15,000 loans in 2012, overtook audiobooks within two years and increased steadily to 110,000 by 2018. Their number then almost doubled to 205,000 in 2020, bringing them within reach of printed books, and despite a minor dip, reached 215,000 in 2024. Audiobooks followed a slower but more consistent upward path. After remaining at around 30,000 for the first two years, their loans rose uninterruptedly to 160,000 by the final year, over five times the 2012 figure.
samples.why: Key features skilfully selected, especially the 2020 turning point · clear, well-placed overview · accurate figures and derived comparisons · precise vocabulary · wide range of structures, virtually error-free.
